Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:11:1.english: For had the Merciful One written [regarding] a seller - That he is enjoined by [the prohibition,] “You shall not exploit.”

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:11:2.hebrew: דקים ליה בזבינתיה - כמה נתן בה, ובמזיד הוא עושה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:11:2.english: Because he is certain of his merchandise - [He knows] how much he paid for it, and he does [so] intentionally.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:12:1.hebrew: זבנת קנית - אם לקחת חפץ המתקיים, שכר הוא אצלך, שלא הוצאת המעות ביציאה והרי הוא מתקיים לך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:12:1.english: You purchased, you acquired - If you bought a lasting item, it is a gain for you, for you did not spend the money on [consumable] expenses, and behold, it endures for you.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:12:2.hebrew: זבין אוביד - מכרת חפץ שלך, הרי אתה נפסד, שיכלו המעות ביציאה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:12:2.english: [One who] sells loses - [If] you sold your item, behold, you lose [out], for the money will be used up on expenses.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:14:1.english: A trader - [One who] buys and sells immediately, constantly.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:14:2.english: He surely knows how much his merchandise is worth - For he did not delay between its purchase and its sale.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:15:1.hebrew: שאפי' פחות מכדי אונאה חוזר - אם נתאנה, דחייו תלויין בכך, ותקנו לו שיחזור:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:15:1.english: As even [for] less than the measure of exploitation, he may retract - If he was exploited, because his livelihood depends on this, and [the Sages] enacted for him that he may retract.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:15:2.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דרב נחמן - דאפי' בכדי אונאה אינו חוזר בו, ואין מחזירין לו אונאה, מדתלי טעמא מפני שהוא בקי, כגון ספסר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:15:2.english: It is taught [in a baraita] in accordance with Rav Nachman - That even for the measure of exploitation, he cannot retract, nor do they return [the] exploitation to him, since it bases the reason on "because he is an expert," such as a broker.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:17:1.english: It teaches: [If he] wishes - That he has the upper hand.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:17:2.english: The baraita - [The baraita] of Rabbi Natan.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:17:3.hebrew: לא קתני רצה - אלא על כרחו קנה, ומחזיר לו אונאה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:17:3.english: [It] does not teach: "[If he] wishes" - Rather, against his will he acquired [it], and he returns the overcharge to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:17:4.hebrew: קתני לוקח - היכא דנתאנה לוקח, קתני דידו על העליונה, כדקתני תן לי מעותי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:17:4.english: [The mishna] teaches [regarding the] buyer - Where the buyer was overcharged, it teaches that he has the upper hand, as it teaches: "Give me my money."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:17:5.english: The baraita - [That is, the baraita] of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:17:6.hebrew: קתני מוכר - דהיכא דנתאנה מוכר, הוא דידו על העליונה; אבל אם נתאנה לוקח, לא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:17:6.english: [It] teaches: "seller" - That where the seller was defrauded, it is he who has the upper hand; but if the buyer was defrauded, [he does] not.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:19:1.english: This exploitation - This Mishnah of ours.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:19:2.hebrew: ותני נמי בברייתא - בר' נתן "רצה", ובלוקח ומוכר הוא דפליגי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:19:2.english: And teach in the baraita as well - In Rabbi Natan's [statement, teach] "wishes," and [thus] it is [only] regarding the buyer and the seller that they disagree.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:19:3.hebrew: דיקא נמי - דמתניתין במוכר נמי ס"ל הכי, ומפרש ללוקח ולא פירש למוכר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:19:3.english: [The language] is also precise - That [the Tanna of] our mishna holds thus regarding the seller as well, yet he explains [the law] for the buyer and did not explain [it] for the seller.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:1:1.hebrew: משום הכי חזרו - שהם היו מוכרין ואינן נהנין בהרחבת זמן החזרה דר' טרפון, שהרי אפי' לרבנן לעולם חוזרים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:1:1.english: Due to this they reverted - For they were sellers, and they do not benefit from Rabbi Tarfon's extension of the time for retraction, since even according to the Rabbis they may always retract.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:1:2.hebrew: אמאי חזרו - לדידהו נמי מהני הרחבת זמן החזרה, דאי טעו אינהו נהדרו בהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:1:2.english: Why did they revert? - For them too, the extension of the time for retraction is beneficial, for if they [themselves] err, they can retract.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:20:1.hebrew: לימא רב דאמר כר' מאיר - דאמר מתנה על מה שכתוב בתורה, תנאו בטל אפילו בדבר שבממון:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:20:1.english: Let us say [that] Rav stated [his opinion] in accordance with Rabbi Meir - Who says [that] one who stipulates contrary to what is written in the Torah, his stipulation is void, even in a monetary matter.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:21:1.hebrew: ר' יהודה אומר בדבר שבממון - כגון שאר וכסות, ניתן למחילה והרי מחלה. אבל עונה, שהיא צער הגוף, לא ניתן למחילה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:21:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: In monetary matters - such as food and clothing, [the obligation] is subject to waiver, and behold, she has waived [it]. However, conjugal rights, which involve physical distress, are not subject to waiver.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:6:1.english: Varshekhei - Silk bands that are called bendels [in Old French].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:6:2.english: He calls out six - [He] asks six zuzim as their price.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:6:3.hebrew: מבעל הבית - תכשיטין וכלי תשמיש שלו חביבין עליו, ואינו מוכרן אלא ביוקר, והוה ליה כמפרש "יודע אני שיש בו אונאה", דאמרינן לקמן "אין לו עליו אונאה". כך מצאתי בשאילתות דרב אחאי (פ' בהר סי' קיג):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:6:3.english: From a homeowner - His jewelry and household utensils are dear to him, and he sells them only at a high price, so it is [considered] as if [the seller] explicitly stated, "I know that there is price exploitation in it," regarding which we say later [that the buyer] has no [claim of] exploitation against him. Thus I found in the She'iltot of Rav Achai (Parashat Behar, sec. 113).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:7:2.hebrew: הוי מחילה - לאלתר, דהוה ליה פחות משתות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:7:2.english: It is a waiver - Immediately, since it is less than a sixth [of the value].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:7:3.english: And I will sue him in court - within [the time] that he may show [it] to a merchant.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:8:1.english: In [the case of] tzadriyyata - [These are] hemp garments that are intended to be sold.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:9:1.hebrew: ר' יהודה אומר אין אונאה לתגר - לקמיה מפרש לה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:9:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: There is no exploitation for a merchant - Later, [the Gemara] explains it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:9:2.english: The one upon whom [it] was imposed - The one who was defrauded.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 51a:9:3.english: Give me my money - If the buyer was overcharged.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 51a:9:1.hebrew: והתנן כשם שאונאה להדיוט כך אונאה לתגר - פירוש: לאפוקי מר' יהודה דאמר: תגר אין לו אונאה כשמכר בזול, לפי שהוא בקי ואחולי אחיל ליה, והאי דזבני' הכי — משום דאתרמי ליה זבינתא אחריתי, כדאמרי' בסמוך. והשתא פריך שפיר, דע"כ מיירי בהדיוט מוכר מדתלי תגר בהדיוט, דטעמא דידע ומחיל לא שייך אלא במוכר. וא"ת: ומנ"ל דמיירי בהדיוט שמוכר ביוקר ונתאנה לוקח, דילמא מיירי בהדיוט שמכר בזול ונתאנה, דהשתא הוי דומיא דתגר? וי"ל: דאונאה משמע בכל ענין, בין שהוא מאנה בין שהוא מתאנה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 51a:9:1.english: "And did we not learn [in the Mishnah]: Just as [the law of] exploitation applies to a layman, so [does the law of] exploitation apply to a merchant?" - Explanation: [This comes] to exclude [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda, who says [that] a merchant has no [claim of] exploitation when he sells cheaply, because he is an expert and waives [the difference], and the reason he sold it like this is because another purchase came his way, as [the Gemara] says shortly. And now [the Gemara] asks well, for perforce [the Mishnah] is speaking of a layman who is a seller, since it links "merchant" to "layman," as the reason that he knows [the value] and waives [it] applies only to a seller. And if you say: But from where do we [know] that [the Mishnah] is speaking of a layman who sells expensively and the buyer was exploited? Perhaps it is speaking of a layman who sold cheaply and was [himself] exploited, so that now it is comparable to [the case of] the merchant? And one can say: That "exploitation" implies in every manner, whether he exploits [another] or he is exploited.
